# FLX-3514: a Kafka topic will not take the stream as it is

**Family:** seam/conformance (the 3000 band)

The record timestamp is the event's time, and the sink never moves a record's bytes to fit a topic. A topic whose message.timestamp.type is LogAppendTime would replace event time with the time of the write, a snapshot's topic must be compacted, and a timestamp outside the topic's message.timestamp.before.max.ms or after.max.ms, or at or below zero (the brokers refuse a negative timestamp and a producer reads 0 as the current time), is refused. An unpaced stream without commit-every is one transaction, and one that cannot finish within transaction-timeout is aborted. A stream the run's own sink-receipts.json says reached the topic of the same cluster, whole or in part (each commit keeps a receipt of the stream so far there), is refused when its topic is still there and the brokers no longer hold its progress (a consumer group's offset, which they drop after offsets.retention.minutes, 7 days by default): sending it again would duplicate what reached the topic, so use another topic-prefix or remove its entry from sink-receipts.json to do that on purpose. Without that local record (another machine, or a removed run directory) a re-send after the retention duplicates. A topic the delivery has to create holds nothing to duplicate, so it is delivered to. The message names the topic and the limit. Configure the topic for the backfill (CreateTime, compaction, wider timestamp limits), choose another topic with --sink-opt topic.EXPOSE=NAME, run a window nearer the present, or for a stream that is too long for one transaction raise transaction-timeout (and the brokers' transaction.max.timeout.ms) or pass commit-every=SECONDS to commit it as it goes.
